# Introduction

There are `r len(biopsies)` lesion biopsies in total, including AS. Different biopsy samples or even different slices from the same biopsy sample may have different amount of lesion tissues. Some completely lack lesion. List of available markers per slide:

\endgroup
\bigskip

Most lesion biopsies have multiple sections. The following choices of representative slides are made: 

```{r results='asis', echo=FALSE}
tab=cbind(
    "Select slide"=sort(select.slides)
    # change shedding rate to genital sweep rate
  , "Sample"=severity [match(get.initial(sort(select.slides)), severity$initial), "ptid", drop=T]
  , "genital_sweep_rate"=severity [match(get.initial(sort(select.slides)), severity$initial), "Shedding.rate", drop=T]
  , "HSV_activity_rate"=severity [match(get.initial(sort(select.slides)), severity$initial), "Activity.rate", drop=T]
  , "PCR_positivity_rate"=formatDouble(100*severity [match(get.initial(sort(select.slides)), severity$initial), "PCR.positivity.rate", drop=T], 1)
)
rownames(tab)=NULL
kable(tab, align = 'c', caption="HSV clinical manifestations.")
```
The key markers are: CD3 CD11c CD123 CD15 CD56 CD68. 

Note that the CD68 antibody stained the epidermis of some tissues. CD68_raw.png is the raw image, and CD68.png is the processed image with reduced epidermis brightness to improve quality of segmentation.

# Correlation with HSV activity rate and shedding rate

Based on the previous report, we decided to 

- focus on normalized counts
- focus on average across slides and select slides and not all slides, which has low correlation
- focus on these metrics
  - DEJ1000, DI
  - DEJ500, DI
  - skin1000, I
  - skin500, I
  - EI
  

Notes on methods:

- Density is the number of cells/mm$^2$. The size of biopsy is on the order of mm$^2$.
- Depth density function is a function of the number of cells per 100x100 um2 tissue over the distance to skin or DEJ in 100 um increment. Each bin in the histogram represents the count in a 100x100 um2 area. 
- Normalized count is the number of cells in a vertical strip 100um wide, and is equivalent to the area under the depth density function (restricted to certain depth if applicable). It is called normalized count because each depth is weighted equally instead of variable depending on the tissue shape. 
- Average slide is computed as the mean norm.counts.
- Ratio is presented as fraction in tables and percentages in graphs. A gap in depth density ratio function is often due to the denominator being 0.
- Ratio for average slides is computed as the ratio of two sums across norm.counts from all slides for the two markers
- R$^2$ is computed without slides from AS_Les, which has the highest shedding rate and appears an outlier.
- The association is done on intact only. Previously we explored association with ulcerative + intact, but decided to focus on intact


**Methods for manuscript**:

Cellular density was quantified as the number of cells per mm². To characterize the spatial distribution of cells across tissue depth, we computed a depth density function defined as the number of cells per 100×100 µm² tissue area as a function of distance from the skin surface or dermal-epidermal junction (DEJ), binned in 100 µm increments. To summarize cellular abundance in a manner that accounts for variable tissue geometry, we computed a normalized count, defined as the number of cells in a vertical strip 100 µm wide, which is equivalent to the area under the depth density function. Gaps in the depth density ratio function reflect bins where the denominator is zero. An average slide was computed as the mean normalized count across slides. For average slides, the ratio was computed as the ratio of summed normalized counts across all slides for the two markers of interest. 



Notes on samples:

- CF1_Les has no CD68
- RC1_Les, RC2_Les, RC3_Les, and RC_Les_avg have no CD123
- SA1_Les, SA2_Les, SA3_Les, and SA_Les_avg have no Foxp3, hence no Treg
- SG1_Les, SG2_Les, SG3_Les, and SG_Les_avg have no Foxp3, hence no Treg


Notes on results:

- Treg counts from JK1_Les and JK3_Les are quite different: 19 and 161. This led the R2 for Treg/CD3 in DI to be higher for select slides than for average slides.

<!-- - Comparing the CD15 cell distribution in CF between intact and ulcerative, we see that the lesion peak is shifted to the left compared to the normal peak. This pattern is more clear in CF than in DD. We don't see this pattern for CD3. -->

```{r correlates, results='asis', echo=FALSE, fig.height=12, fig.width=11, fig.align='center'}

# count_dat comprises a list of slides
# count_dat$AS1_Les is a list of 3 elements: DEJ500, DEJ1000, DEJInf
# count_dat$AS1_Les[['DEJ500']] is a list with 4 columns: sizes, counts, densities, norm.counts
# Similarly, count_dat
xx=c("DEJ1000", "DEJ500", "Skin1000", "Skin500"); names(xx)=xx

cnt.tables=list() # collect first, print tables after plots
for (marker_set in c(1,3,2)) {
for (slide_set in c(1,3)) {
  
  if(slide_set==1) {
    slides=select.slides
  } else if (slide_set==2) {
    slides=all.slides
  } else {
    slides=avg_slides
  }
  
  if (marker_set==1) {
    toplot = key.markers
  } else if (marker_set==2) {
    toplot = ratio_pairs_labels
  } else {
    toplot = c(cell_types)
  }
  
  R2.matrix.ls = list()
  pv.matrix.ls = list()
  for (iter in 1:3) { 
    # 1: association with shedding rate
    # 2: association with HSV activity rate
    # 3: association with PCR positivity rate
    rate = c("Shedding.rate","Activity.rate","PCR.positivity.rate")[iter]
  
    par(mfrow=c(6,length(xx)+1), oma=c(0,0,3,0))
    reduce_margin()
    
    R2.matrix=NULL
    pv.matrix=NULL
    for (a in toplot) {
      
      # make a dataset
      norm.counts=lapply(xx, function (x) {
        # x="Skin500"; a="Treg"
        slides1=slides
        
        # all select slides to have a set of key markers, with the following exceptions:
        if (a=="CD68")  slides1=setdiff(slides, "CF1_Les")
        if (a=="CD123") slides1=setdiff(slides, c("RC3_Les", "RC_Les_avg"))
        
        # No results for Foxp3 for any of the SA and SG slides
        if (a=="Treg")  slides1=setdiff(slides, c("SA1_Les", "SA2_Les", "SA3_Les", "SA_Les_avg",
                                              "SG1_Les", "SG2_Les", "SG3_Les", "SG_Les_avg"))
        
        out = as.data.frame(mysapply(slides1, function (s) {
          ret = count_dat[[s]][[x]]$norm.counts
          if (a %in% colnames(ret)) ret[,a] else stop(glue("{a} is missing for {s}"))
        })); out
        
        slides1 = cbind(
          SR = severity [match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial), rate, drop=T], 
          out,
          initial = get.initial(rownames(out)),
          total=rowSums(out)
        )
        
        slides1[slides1$initial!="AS",] # this removes AS from plot as well
      })
      
      R2 = NULL
      pv = NULL
      
      # scatterplot of normalized densities for dermis intact, because not all tissues have ulcerative
      ylim=NULL
      for (x in c("DEJ1000","DEJ500")){
        fit.lm = lm(DI[initial!="AS"] ~ SR[initial!="AS"], norm.counts[[x]])
        R2 = c(R2, summary(fit.lm)$r.squared); names(R2)[len(R2)] = glue("{x}_DI")
        pv = c(pv, summary(fit.lm)$coef[2,4]); names(pv)[len(pv)] = glue("{x}_DI")
        with(norm.counts[[x]], {
          plot(SR, DI, xlab=rate, main=glue("Normalized Count DI ({x})"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim, cex.main = 0.9, col=match(initial, biopsies), pch=match(initial, biopsies))
          legend("topright", legend=c(
            paste("R2=", round(summary(fit.lm)$r.squared, 3)),
            # extract p value from fit.lm
            paste("p=", formatDouble(summary(fit.lm)$coefficients[2,4], digits=3))
          ), bty="n")
          # add a line for the fit
          abline(fit.lm, col="black", lty=2)
        })
      }
    
      # scatterplot of normalized densities for dermis intact, because not all tissues have ulcerative
      ylim=NULL
      for (x in c("Skin1000","Skin500")){
        fit.lm = lm(I[initial!="AS"] ~ SR[initial!="AS"], norm.counts[[x]])
        R2 = c(R2, summary(fit.lm)$r.squared); names(R2)[len(R2)] = glue("{x}_I")
        pv = c(pv, summary(fit.lm)$coef[2,4]); names(pv)[len(pv)] = glue("{x}_I")
        with(norm.counts[[x]], {
        plot(SR, I, xlab=rate, main=glue("Normalized Count I ({x})"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim, cex.main = 0.9, col=match(initial, biopsies), pch=match(initial, biopsies))
        legend("topright", legend=c(paste("R2=", round(summary(fit.lm)$r.squared, 3)),
          # extract p value from fit.lm
          paste("p=", formatDouble(summary(fit.lm)$coefficients[2,4], digits=3))
        ), bty="n")
        # add a line for the fit
        abline(fit.lm, col="black", lty=2)
      })}
    
      # scatterplot of normalized densities for epidermis intact. does not depend on the DEJ500/DEJ1000/DEJInf
      ylim=NULL
      fit.lm = lm(EI[initial!="AS"] ~ SR[initial!="AS"], norm.counts$DEJ1000)
      R2 = c(R2, summary(fit.lm)$r.squared); names(R2)[len(R2)] = glue("EI")
      pv = c(pv, summary(fit.lm)$coef[2,4]); names(pv)[len(pv)] = glue("EI")
      with(norm.counts$DEJ1000, {
        plot(SR, EI, xlab=rate, main=glue("Normalized Count EI"), ylab=a, ylim=ylim, cex.main = 0.9, col=match(initial, biopsies), pch=match(initial, biopsies))
        legend("topright", legend=c(paste("R2=", round(summary(fit.lm)$r.squared, 3)),
          # extract p value from fit.lm
          paste("p=", formatDouble(summary(fit.lm)$coefficients[2,4], digits=3))
        ), bty="n")
        # add a line for the fit
        abline(fit.lm, col="black", lty=2)
      })
      
      # plot legend only on the first row
      # empty.plot()
      # if (a==toplot[1]) {
      #   mylegend(x=1, pch=1:13, col=1:13, legend=biopsies, cex=.7)
      # }
      
      # create count tables for avg slides
      if (iter==1) # only need to do this once because only cnts not rates are collected
        for (x in xx) cnt.tables = append(cnt.tables, list(
          mykable(round(norm.counts[[x]][, -which (names(norm.counts[[x]]) %in% c("initial", "SR"))], ifelse(marker_set==2,2,0)), 
                caption=paste0(a, ", ", x, ", ", ifelse(slide_set==1, "select slide", "slides average"), ". Normalized counts in different regions: ", ifelse(startsWith(x,"DEJ"), "dermis intact (DI); dermis ulcerative (DU); epidermis intact (EI); epidermis ulcerative (EU)", "intact (I); ulcerative (U)"), ". Total = row sum.")) 
        ))
      
    R2.matrix = cbind(R2.matrix, R2)
    pv.matrix = cbind(pv.matrix, pv)
      
    } # for a: marker
  
    mtext(ifelse(slide_set==3, "Average Slides. ", "Select Slides. ")%.%concatList(toplot, ", "), side = 3, outer = TRUE, line = 2, cex = .9)
    
    cat("\\newpage")
    
    colnames(R2.matrix)=toplot; R2.matrix.ls[[iter]]=R2.matrix
    colnames(pv.matrix)=toplot; pv.matrix.ls[[iter]]=pv.matrix
  } # for iter
  
  # Combine the two matrices
  combined_mat <- cbind(t(R2.matrix.ls[[1]]), t(R2.matrix.ls[[2]]))
  colnames(combined_mat) <- paste0(colnames(combined_mat), rep(c("_Shedding", "_Activity"), each=5))
  combined_mat = combined_mat[,order(colnames(combined_mat))]
  mywrite.csv(formatDouble(combined_mat,3), file=glue("output/csv/R2_{ifelse(slide_set==1,'select','avg')}_marker_set{marker_set}"))
  
  # Combine the two matrices
  combined_mat <- cbind(t(pv.matrix.ls[[1]]), t(pv.matrix.ls[[2]]))
  colnames(combined_mat) <- paste0(colnames(combined_mat), rep(c("_Shedding", "_Activity"), each=5))
  combined_mat = combined_mat[,order(colnames(combined_mat))]
  mywrite.csv(formatDouble(combined_mat,3), file=glue("output/csv/pv_{ifelse(slide_set==1,'select','avg')}_marker_set{marker_set}"))
  
}
}
```

# Multivariate regression with HSV activity rate and shedding rate

Average slides.

```{r covariates adjustment, echo=FALSE, results='asis', fig.height=6, fig.width=6, fig.align='center'}

fits=list(
    lm(Activity.rate~Gender, severity)
  , lm(Activity.rate~Age.at.enrollment, severity)
  , lm(Activity.rate~HSV1, severity)
)

tab=getFormattedSummary(fits, robust=F)
colnames(tab)=c("Gender","Age.at.enrollment","HSV1")
rownames(tab)[2]="Slope"
kable(tab)

myboxplot(Activity.rate~Gender, severity, names=c("Female","Male"))

```

```{r multivariate, echo=FALSE, results='asis', fig.height=6, fig.width=6, fig.align='center'}

slides=avg_slides

R2 <- list(
  Shedding.rate = NULL, 
  Activity.rate = NULL  
)

for (iter in 1:3) { 
  # 1: association with shedding rate
  # 2: association with activity rate
  # 3: association with PCR positivity rate
  rate = c("Shedding.rate","Activity.rate","PCR.positivity.rate")[iter]
  
  cat("\\newpage \n ## ", rate, "\n")
  
  markers = c('CD3','CD11c','CD68','CD56','CD15')

  R2.x = matrix(NA,nr=len(markers),nc=0,dimnames = list(markers,rep("",0)))
  
  for(x in c("DEJ1000", "DEJ500", "Skin1000", "Skin500")) {
    
    norm.counts.ls =  lapply (markers, function(a) {
      # x="Skin500"; a="CD3"
      out = as.data.frame(mysapply(slides, function (s) {
        ret = count_dat[[s]][[x]]$norm.counts
        if (a %in% colnames(ret)) ret[,a] #else stop(glue("{a} is missing for {s}"))
      }))
      
      colnames(out) = colnames(out) %.% "_" %.% a
      
      ret = cbind(
        rate = severity [match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial), rate, drop=T], # rate
        Gender = severity [match(get.initial(rownames(out)), severity$initial), "Gender", drop=T], # rate
        initial = get.initial(rownames(out)),
        out # counts
      )
      
      ret = ret[ret$initial!="AS",] # this removes AS from plot as well
      
      ret
      
    })
    
    # Assume 'my_list' contains your 5 data frames
    norm.counts <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = c("initial","rate","Gender"), all = TRUE), norm.counts.ls)
    
    if (x %in% c("DEJ1000","DEJ500")){
      # DI

      fits = list(
          lm(rate ~ DI_CD3, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD11c, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD68, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD56, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD15, norm.counts)
      )
      tab=matrix(getFormattedSummary(fits, robust=F)[-1,], nc=1,dimnames=list(markers,'single_marker'))
      print(kable(tab, caption = glue("{rate}, DI, {x}")))
      cat("\n\n") # Highly recommended: adds a line break between tables
      
      # add R2
      R2.x = cbind(R2.x, sapply(fits, function (fit) summary(fit)$r.squared))
      colnames(R2.x)[ncol(R2.x)]=x
        
      fits = list(
          lm(rate ~ DI_CD3 + DI_CD11c, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD3 + DI_CD68, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD3 + DI_CD56, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD3 + DI_CD15, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD11c + DI_CD68, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD11c + DI_CD56, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD11c + DI_CD15, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD68 + DI_CD56, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD68 + DI_CD15, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ DI_CD56 + DI_CD15, norm.counts)
      )
      tab=t(getFormattedSummary(fits, robust=F)[-1,])
      colnames(tab)=c("Marker1","Marker2")
      print(kable(tab, caption = glue("{rate}, DI, {x}")))
      
      mypairs(norm.counts[, startsWith(names(norm.counts), "DI")])
      cat("\n\n\\clearpage") # Highly recommended: adds a line break between tables
      
    } else if (x %in% c("Skin1000","Skin500")){
      # I

      fits = list(
          lm(rate ~ I_CD3, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD11c, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD68, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD56, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD15, norm.counts)
      )
      tab=matrix(getFormattedSummary(fits, robust=F)[-1,], nc=1,dimnames=list(markers,'single_marker'))
      print(kable(tab, caption = glue("{rate}, I, {x}")))
      cat("\n\n") # Highly recommended: adds a line break between tables
      
      # add R2
      R2.x = cbind(R2.x, sapply(fits, function (fit) summary(fit)$r.squared))
      colnames(R2.x)[ncol(R2.x)]=x

      fits = list(
          lm(rate ~ I_CD3 + I_CD11c, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD3 + I_CD68, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD3 + I_CD56, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD3 + I_CD15, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD11c + I_CD68, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD11c + I_CD56, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD11c + I_CD15, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD68 + I_CD56, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD68 + I_CD15, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ I_CD56 + I_CD15, norm.counts)
      )
      tab=t(getFormattedSummary(fits, robust=F)[-1,])
      colnames(tab)=c("Marker1","Marker2")
      print(kable(tab, caption = glue("{rate}, I, {x}")))
      
      mypairs(norm.counts[, startsWith(names(norm.counts), "I")])
      cat("\n\n\\clearpage") # Highly recommended: adds a line break between tables

    } 
    
    
    if (x %in% c("DEJ1000")){
      # EI
      fits = list(
          lm(rate ~ EI_CD3, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD11c, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD68, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD56, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD15, norm.counts)
      )
      tab=matrix(getFormattedSummary(fits, robust=F)[-1,], nc=1,dimnames=list(markers,'single_marker'))
      print(kable(tab, caption = glue("{rate}, EI"))) # no need to put x in title because it is epidermis, not affected by depth
      cat("\n\n") # Highly recommended: adds a line break between tables
      
      # add R2
      R2.x = cbind(R2.x, sapply(fits, function (fit) summary(fit)$r.squared))
      colnames(R2.x)[ncol(R2.x)]="EI"

      fits = list(
          lm(rate ~ EI_CD3 + EI_CD11c, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD3 + EI_CD68, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD3 + EI_CD56, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD3 + EI_CD15, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD11c + EI_CD68, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD11c + EI_CD56, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD11c + EI_CD15, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD68 + EI_CD56, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD68 + EI_CD15, norm.counts)
        , lm(rate ~ EI_CD56 + EI_CD15, norm.counts)
      )
      tab=t(getFormattedSummary(fits, robust=F)[-1,])
      colnames(tab)=c("Marker1","Marker2")
      print(kable(tab, caption = glue("{rate}, EI, {x}")))
 
      mypairs(norm.counts[, startsWith(names(norm.counts), "EI")])
      cat("\n\n\\clearpage") # Highly recommended: adds a line break between tables

    }
  }
      
  R2[[iter]] = R2.x
}
```
